https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/223.text: Home News World Andrew Tate (R) and Tristan Tate (L) have been arrested in Miami (Image: Getty) Andrew Tate and his brother have been arrested in the United States following an investigation by police into a number of alleged sexual offences. The influencers who have millions of followers on social media were arrested yesterday (Saturday, July 18) in Miami. Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 38, have been detained pending ongoing legal proceedings as 38 new charges have been authorised against the pair. Charges were previously authorised by CPS following a file of evidence submitted by officers from Bedfordshire Police into allegations dating back to 2012. Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT The brothers face 38 new charges (Image: Getty) Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire Major Crime Unit have been continuing to investigate a number of other offences reported to both Bedfordshire Police and Hertfordshire Constabulary. The total number of charges against the brothers now totals 59. Of these, 42 charges have been authorised against Andrew Tate, and 17 against Tristan Tate. Assistant Chief Constable Karena Thomas said: “Officers from our major crime unit have been working closely alongside the Crown Prosecution Service and both national and international law enforcement agencies as part of this complex investigation. “We understand the interest that this case will generate, but we would urge the public not to speculate and to allow the legal process to be carried out correctly. There is no place for male violence against women and girls, and we will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us.” Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said it had requested the extradition of Andrew and Tristan Tate from the US. Read our Privacy Policy Malcolm McHaffie, head of the CPS’s Special Crime Division, said: “We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offences including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child. “These charging decisions followed receipt of a further file of evidence from Bedfordshire Police and bring the total number of alleged victims in this case to seven.” The CPS said the offending is alleged to have taken place between July 2010 and August 2017. He added: “The CPS has requested the extradition of the Tates from the US. They have been arrested and await extradition proceedings to the UK.” The brothers are facing legal proceedings in Romania, where they currently live, and were facing extradition to the UK upon their completion after Bedfordshire Police secured European arrest warrants for the pair in 2024. The pair have previously “unequivocally” denied wrongdoing, with Andrew Tate describing himself and his brother as “very innocent men”. In June, their bid to bring a legal challenge against the CPS after it did not disclose the names of their alleged victims in UK criminal proceedings was thrown out by a High Court judge. The attack also damaged warehouse facilities and at least 12 vehicles. In a separate incident, a strike in the Bucha district injured three people and caused a fire at an industrial facility. These daytime attacks followed a massive barrage involving 35 missiles and 185 drones, during which a critical shortage of Patriot interceptors allowed ballistic missiles to inflict severe casualties and infrastructure damage in Kyiv and other regions. by Tymur Dubovyk | Aug. 1, 2026, 2:16 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied The State Emergency Service is extinguishing a fire caused by a Russian drone attack on the Kyiv region, Aug. 1. (Photo by the State Emergency Service of Ukraine/Telegram) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip A daytime Russian drone attack struck a logistics center belonging to the e-commerce company Rozetka in Brovary, Kyiv region, on Saturday, Aug. 1, killing one person and injuring six others. According to the Kyiv Regional Prosecutor’s Office , the drone struck the marketplace’s warehouse facilities at approximately 11:28 a.m. local time. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . The attack killed a 61-year-old man and left six people wounded, with one individual reported to be in serious condition. Kyiv Regional Military Administration head Tymur Tkachenko confirmed the strike on the warehouse premises, adding that at least 12 vehicles were damaged in the blast. The State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) reported that rescue teams provided medical assistance to all the victims and continued operations to mitigate the aftermath of the attack. Advertisement In a separate daytime incident, the DSNS reported that a Russian strike caused a fire at an industrial facility in the Bucha district, leaving three people injured. Fire and rescue units, alongside specialized robotic equipment, were deployed to extinguish the blaze. Massive overnight attack on Kyiv The daytime drone attacks on the Kyiv region followed a massive nationwide aerial barrage early Saturday morning that involved a total of 35 missiles and 185 attack drones of various types. During the assault, Ukrainian air defenses intercepted just one of 27 Russian ballistic missiles due to a critical shortage of Patriot interceptors. Other Topics of Interest Ukraine Strikes Crimean Rail Bridges and Naval Drone Depot Ukrainian forces struck two railway bridges, a naval drone depot, and a Black Sea Fleet intelligence unit in Crimea, the military reported. While strikes were also recorded in Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk, Sumy, Kharkiv, and Poltava regions, the capital was the primary target of the ballistic missiles. The strikes on Kyiv triggered repeated explosions, killing nine residents and injuring 30 others, including four children, according to the Kyiv City Military Administration. The attacks damaged 18 apartment and private residential buildings, a medical clinic, a film studio, supermarkets, and several vehicles, including a depot where 25 ambulances were destroyed or damaged. The building housing the Lithuanian embassy also sustained damage during the bombardment. Advertisement President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the interception failure regarding the ballistic missiles , stating that the deficit of interceptor stockpiles actively encourages further strikes. He urged international partners to expedite the delivery of anti-ballistic systems to prevent further loss of life.
